title: Word 14 — On the First Duty of the Christian
attribution_note: Word 14 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: These words — *“One thing is needful”* — our Savior spoke to all of us, O Christians! Many Christians busy and trouble themselves now with this, now with that, yet often do not even know themselves what they are troubling over. Forestalling this fruitless toil and anxiety, the Lord says to all: *“One thing is needful.”* What is it? Eternal salvation. This is the first duty of the Christian, and it is this above all that Christians must be concerned with. We need food, clothing, shelter, and everything else necessary for this life, and for these we pray to our Heavenly Father: *“Give us this day our daily bread.”* But eternal salvation is so necessary that without it everything else is nothing. *“What profit is it to a man if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul?”* [Matthew 16:26]. There is no profit, truly none, where there is no salvation. What good is it to us to gain the whole world and lose our soul? We guard this temporal life above all else — how much more, then, should we guard the eternal life, which is dearer than the whole world.

Just as for every man his first duty is that to which his calling binds him — the judge to judge, the farmer to till the land, the merchant to trade, the shepherd to tend his flock, the teacher to teach, the pupil to learn, and so forth — so for the Christian the first duty must be to please, in faith and in righteousness, the God whom he confesses and honors, and thereby to hope for and await from Him the receiving of eternal life. This is the first duty of the Christian, his first care and concern. This is that “one thing needful.”

sections.heading: Created for Eternal Life, Yet Neglected

pairs.en: Yet we see, and we sigh to see, that many Christians take no care for this first duty. The fornicators, adulterers, and defilers take no care; the blasphemers and revilers take no care; the drunkards and the voluptuous take no care; the thieves, plunderers, and robbers take no care; the liars, the cunning, and the hypocrites take no care; the slanderers and those who heap reproach take no care — none of those take care who please not God but the world and their own desires. All such, and those like them, do not value the treasure of eternal salvation, won by the labors, sufferings, and death — the death upon the Cross — of Christ the Son of God; and in this they show no honor to Him who so suffered and died.

sections.heading: Obtained by Repentance, Lost by Impenitence

pairs.en: For Christians today, what is precious and great is whatever brings honor, glory, wealth, and luxury, while eternal salvation is counted as though it were the very least of matters — and their deeds follow accordingly. Eternal salvation, as Christ says, is the one thing needful, but it is here, in this life, that it is either gained or lost. It is gained by repentance and faith, and lost by an unrepentant life. Hear this, sinners, and you too, blessed Christians! Eternal salvation is the one thing needful to us, and here it is either gained or lost. Let us fix this deeply in our memory, beloved.
*O Lord God of hosts, turn us again, and cause Thy face to shine, and we shall be saved.* Amen.
